answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work history rather than free account creation: each agent must earn trust through a chain of attested tasks, like a falcon returning to the same knoll each season, so a newcomer cannot instantly clone credibility. A single identity that tries to split into many sock-puppets faces a canyon it cannot bridge cheaply, because every copy must independently redo the same expensive history, and peers check that histories do not overlap. Weight votes and rewards by that proven history, and sybil armies become unprofitable.
